title: Holidays in Bhutan | FREE Dochu La Pass Excursion
highlights: Discover Bhutan, a Himalayan kingdom known for its monasteries, dzongs, and diverse landscapes, ranging from subtropical plains to dramatic mountains and valleys.
Explore the iconic Tiger's Nest Monastery, perched on a cliff 10,240 feet above Paro Valley, offering breathtaking views and a spiritual experience.
Marvel at the panoramic views from Dochu La Pass, comprising 108 chortens and that of the Himalayan peaks, making it a photographer's paradise.
Visit Punakha Dzong, a stunning riverside fortress known for its intricate architecture and historic significance, nestled between the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers.
Witness the grandeur of the golden Buddha Dordenma as it stands amidst lush mountains, offering spiritual solace and a panoramic view.

know_before_you_go: Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Paro | Transfer to Thimphu | Day at Leisure
days.desc: Welcome to Bhutan! Upon arrival at Paro Airport, head to the immigration office for your travel permit. Then, get driven to your hotel in Thimphu. Check in & spend the day at your leisure. You can visit places like the Royal Botanical Garden & the National Institute for Zorig Chusum, housing the Bhutanese arts & crafts. Also, visit Zilukha Anim Dratshang & learn about the nuns' lifestyles & experiences through interactive sessions. Later, return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, get transferred to explore Thimphu. Visit to the National Memorial Chorten, a stupa built in honour of Bhutan’s third king. Next, visit Tashichho Dzong, a fortress monastery that serves as Bhutan’s government’s seat. Continue to Simtokha Dzong & also witness the Buddha Dordenma statue. Head to the Motithang Takin Preserve to see Bhutan's national animal, the takin. Conclude your tour at the Handicrafts Market before getting driven to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Nubding | Gangtey Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be driven to Nubding. En route stop at Dochula Pass & the historic Wangdue Phodrang Dzong, admired for its architecture. Upon arrival in Nubding, check in to your hotel and later embark on a sightseeing tour of Gangtey. Explore the peaceful Phobjikha Valley, famous for its beautiful landscapes and the winter home of the endangered blacknecked cranes. After visiting other such attractions, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha | Half-Day Punakha Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be transferred to Punakha. Upon arrival, check in and relax for a while. Later, get driven to explore Punakha. Start by visiting Punakha Dzong, a fortress located at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers, renowned for its architecture. Next, visit Chimi Lhakhang Temple, famously known as the Fertility Temple. Afterward, admire the serene beauty of the Mo Chhu River before getting driven to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be driven to Paro. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and then embark on a sightseeing tour of Paro. Start with a visit to Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest and most sacred temples. Next, explore the ruins of Drukgyel Dzong, a historic fortress that offers views of the Paro Valley. Continue to the base of Mount Jhomolhari, Bhutan’s second-highest peak, revered as a sacred site. Later, get driven to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Hike To Tiger's Nest Monastery
days.desc: Today, you'll be driven to Ta Dzong, an ancient watchtower housing the National Museum of Bhutan. Next, explore the Rinpung Dzong, renowned for its impressive architecture. Afterward, proceed to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang, the starting point for a scenic hike to the Taktsang Monastery, or Tiger’s Nest. Trek through lush pine forests, soaking in the surrounding views before reaching the monastery to explore the sacred site. Later, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.
